title: How Much Does It Cost to Replace Carpet With Vinyl Plank in Seattle?
meta: Replacing carpet with vinyl plank in Seattle costs $2.50 per sq ft in labor at Wills Flooring, plus plank, removal and $100 per stair. See real job math here.

blocks.lead: Replacing carpet with vinyl plank in Seattle costs $2.50 per sq ft in installation labor at Wills Flooring, plus $100 per stair, with a 500 sq ft minimum. Carpet removal, the plank itself and any subfloor prep are separate lines quoted at the free estimate.
blocks.detail: A typical 700 sq ft Seattle upstairs with 13 carpeted stairs comes to $1,750 + $1,300 = $3,050 in labor before material and removal. Most whole-floor carpet-to-LVP jobs in Seattle land between the low four figures and the mid four figures all in, depending on the plank you pick.

blocks.html: This is the most common flooring job in Seattle right now: pull the 15-year-old carpet out of a West Seattle upstairs or a Beacon Hill rental and put down vinyl plank. People ask the price on Google, get quotes from $4 to $12 per square foot "installed" and cannot tell what is inside those numbers. Below is every line that shows up on a real carpet-to-LVP invoice, with our published rates where we publish them and an honest note where the number depends on your house.

blocks.text: What changes the price in a Seattle house

items.title: What is under the carpet
items.text: In Ballard and Wallingford houses from the 1920s to 1950s, carpet often covers original fir or oak. If we find hardwood, we tell you, because refinishing it may be the better move. Newer homes have plywood or OSB, which is the easy case.

items.title: Flatness
items.text: Carpet hides a lot. A settled 1940s floor in Magnolia can have a half-inch dip that vinyl plank will telegraph and click apart over. Leveling compound is the most common prep line on old Seattle houses.

items.title: Stairs
items.text: Stairs are the single biggest swing. A 13-step flight is $1,300 in labor plus nosings. Some Seattle families keep carpet on the stairs and run plank everywhere else to save it.

items.title: Condos and access
items.text: Capitol Hill and Belltown buildings need an acoustic underlayment that meets the HOA sound rating, an elevator reservation and quiet hours. None of that is expensive, but it has to be planned.

blocks.text: Should you pull the carpet yourself?

a.title: Makes sense when
items: It is one or two rooms on the main floor with no stairs
You have a truck or a transfer station run planned; Seattle garbage pickup will not take rolled carpet
You are willing to pull every staple and the tack strip too
You want to see the subfloor before we quote prep

b.title: Better when
items: There are stairs; stair carpet is stapled every few inches
The carpet is glued down over plywood or slab
You are in a condo with elevator and disposal rules
You would rather have one crew responsible for the whole floor

blocks.html: If you do pull it yourself, leave the tack strip if you are unsure how to remove it cleanly; we will handle it. Do pull the staples. A subfloor with 300 pad staples left in it is not ready for plank, and cleaning it up is the part of removal that takes the longest. Before you start, it is worth reading what you might find under the carpet, because hardwood under there changes the whole plan.

blocks.text: When replacing carpet with vinyl plank is the wrong move

blocks.title: Check for hardwood first:
blocks.text: Roughly one in four pre-1960 Seattle homes we visit has solid oak or fir under the carpet. Refinishing that floor costs $3.99 per sq ft all-in at our published natural rate and adds more resale value than any vinyl plank. Lift a corner in a closet before you buy a single box of LVP.

items.html: Second floors where sound matters. Carpet is the quietest floor there is. Vinyl plank over a bedroom above a living room needs a good acoustic underlayment or the footsteps will be heard below.
Rooms over an unheated Seattle crawlspace. Carpet and pad insulate. Plank does not. The room will feel colder underfoot in January unless the crawlspace is sealed or the underlayment adds R-value.
A nursery or playroom you will re-carpet in five years anyway. Some families prefer soft floors while kids are small and switch later. Both are fine; just do not pay twice.
Selling in six months. Fresh carpet in a bedroom is cheaper than plank and buyers accept it. Plank pays off when you live on it.

blocks.text: How to get an accurate quote the first time

items: Measure each room roughly and count the stairs before you call. It lets us bring the right samples and give you a real range on the phone.
Lift a corner of carpet in a closet and photograph what is under it.
Decide whether the baseboards stay. Quarter round is cheaper; pulling and resetting baseboards looks cleaner.
Ask for the plank's wear layer and core type in writing. A 20 mil rigid-core plank is the standard for Seattle rentals and family homes.
Ask what happens if the subfloor needs leveling. It should be a written line before the job, not a surprise on install day.
Get labor, material, removal, stairs and transitions as separate lines from a licensed installer with a workmanship warranty. Ours is one year.

faq.q: How much does it cost to replace carpet with vinyl plank in a 1,000 sq ft Seattle house?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rate, 1,000 sq ft is $2,500 in installation labor. Add the plank you choose, carpet removal, any leveling and $100 for each stair. A mid-grade rigid-core plank typically brings a job this size into the mid four figures all in.

faq.q: Does the $2.50 per sq ft include removing the old carpet?
faq.a: No. Carpet and pad removal, tack strip, staple cleanup and haul-away are quoted separately at the free estimate because the effort depends on stairs, glue and square footage. Some customers remove it themselves; we still need the staples out before we install.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank go directly over the carpet pad or subfloor?
faq.a: Over the subfloor, yes, once staples and tack strips are gone and it is flat within about 3/16 in over 10 ft. Never over carpet or pad. A thin underlayment or a plank with an attached pad goes between the plank and the plywood.

faq.q: How long does a carpet-to-vinyl-plank job take?
faq.a: One day for 600 to 800 sq ft with no stairs, including removal. Add a day for a full staircase and another if the subfloor needs leveling and cure time. You can walk on click-lock plank immediately and move furniture back the same evening.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to replace carpet with new carpet or with vinyl plank?
faq.a: New carpet is usually cheaper up front for a bedroom. Vinyl plank costs more on day one, lasts two to three times longer, and is what Seattle tenants and buyers now expect in halls and living areas. For rentals, plank wins on total cost over ten years.

faq.q: Do I need a permit or HOA approval in Seattle?
faq.a: No city permit for flooring. Condos and townhomes usually require notice to the HOA, an acoustic underlayment that meets the building's sound standard, and an elevator reservation. We handle the underlayment spec and schedule around quiet hours.
